## Ticket proposals
- **Bash hook: a brace group after coproc, time or ! hides a zsh short loop or short conditional** — suggested P2; created as [[SPD-081]] at P2 by Spud.
  Why: A brace group after coproc, time or ! is flattened into the command's words, so ShellWalk never opens a frame for it and a zsh short loop or short conditional inside it is never read. `{ repeat 1 git push }` on its own is read (the git push is found), but `coproc { repeat 1 git push }`, `coproc { if [[ -n x ]] git push }`, `time { repeat 1 git push; }` and `! { repeat 1 git push; }` are all kind other with no finding, and zsh 5.9 runs the push in every one of them. The same flattening is what keeps a cd inside `coproc { cd /tmp; }` from moving the line's directory (SPD-054), so the fix is not simply to push a group frame: the group needs a frame whose effect is still the coproc's fork. Not fixed here: SPD-060 is about the NAME before a compound command, and the prefix-word path is a separate reading.
  Evidence: Probed in zsh 5.9 -f and zsh -f -o nobareglobqual with a fake git first on a scratch PATH, and dumped through analyse_command on this branch with all three of SPD-061, SPD-059 and SPD-060 in place. Ran the push once each in both zsh readings: `coproc { repeat 1 git push }`, `coproc { repeat 1 git push; }`, `coproc { if [[ -n x ]] git push }`, `coproc { for f (a) git push }`, `time { repeat 1 git push; }`, `! { repeat 1 git push; }`. The hook reads every one of them as kinds=other findings=[], while the same group with no prefix word, `{ repeat 1 git push }`, is kinds=git findings=[('git', ('push', 'push'))]. bash 3.2 has no coproc and rejects the zsh-only forms. In ShellWalk.add_word the `{` only opens a group when self.words is empty; after `coproc`, `time` or `!` it is appended as an ordinary word, and analyse_words then strips it as a reserved word and reads the rest as one simple command. SPD-042's sibling branch does open a frame for `for`, `select` and `repeat` after those words, and SPD-061 has just added `if`, `while` and `until` there; `{` is the one left.
